components: Two independent four-ticket F5 sources supply only terminal raw phases to an arbitrary co-located positive comparator. Common rotation and randomized orientation reduce the all-pairs responses to four nonnegative distance rates; neither Bell separation nor individual device symmetry is assumed.

The homogeneous witness 6q2-4q3-5q0 is nonpositive, while the supplied pure-qubit antisymmetric comparison benchmark gives 1/4. The absolute all-pairs maximum-coordinate discrepancy is at least 1/36, attained by literal five-tag circuits using an independent 7:2 schedule.
All prepared pairs count. Shared skip records can fake the target and omitting orientation randomization invalidates the witness; these are resource controls, not experimental observations.
candidates.declared_status: Exact comparator bound for independent raw-phase inputs and a supplied quantum benchmark, not an experimental exclusion of F5 primitives or a physical qubit preparation.
missing_bridges: Certify independent preparations and absence of preparation labels, shared skip records and correlated auxiliary stock at the comparator.
Establish the actual flag readout, setting randomization, efficiencies and any error budget before applying the finite witness to physical data; the quantum reference is supplied.

sources.text:
"""Can two independent F5 preparations reproduce an unknown-state comparator?

An experimenter may hand both signals to ONE arbitrary co-located device:
there is no Bell separation assumption here. Two independent four-ticket
sources P_n and P_m send only their terminal raw phases. No preparation
labels, skip records, shared skip bits or correlated auxiliary stock may
reach the comparator. Common shifts and orientations are averaged with
known settings; *every* prepared pair is counted. The benchmark is a
supplied quantum antisymmetric measurement on two independent pure qubits,
not a claim that either source already sends qubits.

Barnett, Chefles & Jex https://doi.org/10.1016/S0375-9601(02)01602-X
give the quantum state-comparison setting. Hendrych et al.
https://doi.org/10.1016/S0375-9601(03)00262-7 measured photon polarization
overlap using symmetric/antisymmetric optical projections. They did not
implement this F5 preparation or our input-independence certificate.
"""
